description: Counts of how American wire-style news stories are written: sentence and lead length, paragraph length, how often a sentence quotes someone, attribution words and sentence openers. Counts and one- to three-word tokens only; no sentence from a story ships.

source.document: Voice of America staff news stories
source.publisher: Voice of America, U.S. Agency for Global Media
source.license: Public domain (work of the U.S. government); stories naming a wire service skipped

coverage: 51 VOA staff stories published 2024-08-29 to 2026-10-06, taken from every VOA English RSS feed on 2026-10-06.

mining.sentenceRule: A sentence ends at a period, question mark or exclamation point followed by a capital letter or an opening quote.
